stations.name: What it covers
stations.meaning: Which hazard, which asset, which parts; what is left out
stations.paragraph: Wildfire on solar farms: exact-class state tables per part on FSim flame-length classes; ordering constrained by field, lab and guidance sources, absolute values set by engineering judgment. It names 10 parts: PV modules, Tracker and racking, Piles and inverter pads, Central inverters, Combiner boxes, Exposed AC and DC cable, Transformers and switchgear, Grounding and lightning protection, SCADA and communications and Civil: fencing, roads, buildings, site prep. Outside its scope: equipment-origin fire and battery storage, power shutoffs, downtime, business interruption and insurance terms, post-fire erosion or landslide, environmental remediation and fire-service liability and soft and non-physical cost (installed capex above physical replacement value). Kinds of damage it does not include: smoke and ash optical losses and module cleaning.

stations.name: What breaks
stations.meaning: The parts of the plant the hazard damages, each with its own curve
stations.paragraph: For this hazard the solar farm is split into 10 parts: PV modules, Tracker and racking, Piles and inverter pads, Central inverters, Combiner boxes, Exposed AC and DC cable, Transformers and switchgear, Grounding and lightning protection, SCADA and communications and Civil: fencing, roads, buildings, site prep. Parts of the plant's value with no curve yet: replacement support and fieldwork: no own curve; allocated once at the aggregate direct-and-civil damage ratio (T4 rule).

stations.name: How damage is measured
stations.meaning: The hazard intensity on the x-axis and the shape of the curve
stations.paragraph: Damage is read against FSim conditional flame-length class (0 = no event). The curve is a table of damage ratios at exact classes, nothing in between. The input, in the catalogue's words: USFS FSim conditional flame-length class, exact integer 1 to 6 (0 = no event), or the six-class probability vector; no interpolation; burn probability stays with Hazard.

stations.name: Where the numbers come from
stations.meaning: The sources, what was taken from each, and how sure we are
stations.paragraph: 21 sources set this cell: USDA Forest Service, Spatial datasets of probabilistic wildfire risk components for the US, 3rd ed., RDS-2016-0034-3, DOE/FEMP, Solar Photovoltaic Hardening for Resilience - Wildfire, NEMA GD 2-2016, Evaluating Fire- and Heat-Damaged Electrical Equipment and FM, Data Sheet 7-106: Ground-Mounted Solar Power, April 2026 and 17 more. Of the 9 parameters, 3 are lab-tested (T2) and 6 are our judgment (T4). The source and claim registers are machine-readable files in the cell folder. 1 source has no link in the register.
stations.plain_fact: 21 sources · lab-tested, transferred and our judgment

stations.name: What it is worth
stations.meaning: The share of the plant's value the curves cover
stations.paragraph: The damage ratio is a share of pre-event direct replacement value of the same part; the plant view uses the named reference profile WILDFIRE_SOLAR_REFERENCE_100MWDC_V1 or complete site part values. The files state no plant-level dollar figure for this asset. Shares of the plant's physical value, as the cell states them: PV modules 33 %, Tracker and racking 13 %, Piles and inverter pads 4 %, Central inverters 4 %, Combiner boxes 1 %, Exposed AC and DC cable 8 %, Transformers and switchgear 12 %, Grounding and lightning protection 1 %, SCADA and communications 0 % and Civil: fencing, roads, buildings, site prep 4 %.

stations.name: The audit
stations.meaning: The seven checks a curve passes before release
stations.paragraph: No seven-step audit was found as a file or as a section of the dossier. That is a finding, not an omission of the page. A site-condition adapter exists as a file.

stations.name: The files
stations.meaning: The runtime file, the write-up and the workbook
stations.paragraph: The runtime file is the curve artifact with 10 curve records (model v1.0, docs r3). The write-up is wildfire_solar_curve_derivation_dossier__model_v1_0__docs_r3.md. The workbook is damage_curve_records_wildfire_solar__model_v1_0__docs_r3.xlsx. The cell folder holds 12 files, each with its SHA under Details.

stations.name: What it can output
stations.meaning: What a consumer may compute with this curve
stations.paragraph: It can give one wildfire event. A dollar scenario, yearly loss and PML, VaR and TVaR are available only under conditions the consumer (Hazard) checks. Annual metrics belong to the consumer; nothing here is an expected annual loss.

stations.name: How it was tested
stations.meaning: The known answers this build reproduced
stations.paragraph: This build reproduced 26 of 26 known answers through the cell's evaluator (within 1e-12 on the damage ratio). 3 were not run: runtime request-contract tests (frequency field, value-profile requirement, mitigation credit) belong to the cell validator; the build samples curves. The validation record says report. 1 outside check: Financial range check (Hazard repo): industry loss figures for solar wildfire.

claims.text: FSim defines six Fire Intensity Levels and corresponding conditional flame-length-probability layers: FLP1 <2 ft; FLP2 2–<4; FLP3 4–<6; FLP4 6–<8; FLP5 8–<12; FLP6 ≥12 ft.
claims.locator: RDS abstract and entity/attribute definitions for FLP1–FLP6

claims.text: The six FLPs sum to one conditional on burning. For pixels burned in simulation they represent proportions by flame-length bin; metadata-described unburned burnable pixels receive zonal-mean FLPs and nominal BP, so the metadata-defined imputation state must be preserved or detected.
claims.locator: Entity and Attribute Information — Conditional Flame-Length Probability; logical-consistency checks; process step 11 post-processing

claims.text: Annual burn probability is separate from conditional severity and remains outside M3 damage.
FSim FLPs do not provide component heat flux, exposure duration, flame contact, ember dose or damage.
claims.update_trigger: new official product supplies target exposure

claims.text: Fireline intensity is energy release per fire-front length and depends on heat yield, consumed fuel and spread rate.
Legacy q = 0.35·I/d is not a governed converter.
A fixed 10 m fire-to-asset distance is not a default.
No continuous FLI midpoint or FIL6 upper cap is reconstructed from source-native FIL bins.
Tested shielded PV specimens primarily tolerated 8–15 kW/m² and 61–84 °C maximum temperature difference before reported failure behavior.
Tested small PV modules had empirical sustained-flame ignition CHF near 26 kW/m².
PV ignition times were 913/636/218/133/83 s at 28/30/35/40/45 kW/m² for the tested specimens.
Tested 9 mm XLPE cable construction had estimated ignition CHF 16.24 kW/m².
Mean XLPE ignition times were 83.5/25/13.3 s at 20/30/40 kW/m².
Front-glass integrity materially affected full-size single-glass module burn-through and temperature response under tested pool-fire exposure.
Tilt effect was non-monotonic in the tested pool-fire configuration and peaked at 15°.
Fire/ember exposure should be uncoupled from construction vulnerability and quantified in space and time.
Vegetation management, undergrounding where practical, fire-resistant containers, access and emergency planning are PV-relevant risk controls.
Noncombustible screens/barriers may interrupt flame spread, but the effect is geometry- and pathway-dependent.
Combustible fences can rapidly conduct fire; fence-plus-mulch and parallel-fence configurations can increase hazard disproportionately.
Noncombustible fencing still requires maintenance to prevent accumulated fine fuels.
Grass height near electrical equipment should be no more than 100 mm during the declared Fire Danger Period in the cited Victoria control framework.
The cited Victoria framework calls for at least 10 m fuel-free noncombustible firebreaks around key infrastructure and the perimeter.
The cited NSW operational guidance disallows firefighting within 8 m of large-scale generation infrastructure or a fenced area without explicit de-energization assurance.
Module/combiner conductors are commonly exposed while direct burial, conduit and trays are distinct installation states.
Residential defensible-space effectiveness varied by distance and site context; it is transfer evidence only.
Reference installed basis is 1120.000000 USD/kWdc.
